prior_importants.description: unthreadedImportants subtracts one for every `- `path:N` (` line that follows any line shaped like a carried count header, with no limit and no dedupe. Finding text inside the summary body can contain such lines at column 0, so it can push the count of unthreaded importants to zero and release a PR to `ready` while an important it carried is still unthreaded. The workflow comment says finding text 'could only hold a PR in review'; that is no longer true.

findings.description: An unanchored important that the operator accepts as declined holds the PR in review-open for good, with no operator action that clears it. The trigger is an important with no line in this diff to anchor to (say, on a caller in an untouched file) that the author declines. It never gets a thread, so it has no resolve-to-accept path. Every later incremental round copies it forward as `unresolved`: the SKILL's §3 says an important is never deferred, and the code at head is unchanged. So `unthreadedImportants` counts it on every summary from then on. ADR 0165 calls exactly this outcome a defect for carried entries that have a thread, and its fix covers only those. It does not say that unanchored or location-unrecorded entries keep the label on with no override; the ADR should say so or give them a way out.

`botThreads` never reads who resolved a thread. Anyone allowed to resolve a conversation can do it, and that includes an outside author of a fork PR, not only the operator. So such an author can resolve the round-1 bot thread on an important. That ends its hold through `threads.some(!isResolved)`, as on the base. The change adds one more effect: line 116 now also drops the incremental round's carried entry for that important from `unthreadedImportants`, so the PR is labelled `ready` while the newest verdict summary still lists it as "still open". ADR 0165 assumes this resolve is the operator accepting a declined finding. A fix would read `resolvedBy { login }` in the GraphQL query and only treat a resolved thread as releasing when the operator (or an insider) resolved it.
